expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | { status: "trialing"; ... } | { status: "active"; ... } | { status: "past_due"; ... } | { status: "canceled"; ... }

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each variant lists exactly its own fields; canceled has only `cancellation`, trialing only `trial_end_date`

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never): never { ... } ... default: return assertNever(sub);

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Branding is applied only to dates (TrialEndDate, RenewalDate, GracePeriodEnd); no ID field or branded ID type appears anywhere in the design

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function is given; only offered at the end — "Would you like me to ... add state transition functions"

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "Misuse enumeration" list plus table: "Trialing subscription with retry_count | Property doesn't exist on that variant"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "The hazard here is C8: bag-of-optionals"; primary recommendation is the discriminated union
